correctness.rationale: For real symmetric singular H positive semidefinite and delta>0, orthogonal decomposition z=z_R+z_N, b=b_R+b_N, Range(H) perpendicular ker(H) isolates the nullspace: constraint ignores z_N, so b_N!=0 gives the explicit feasible recession ray z_N=-s b_N and objective to -infinity regardless of a. For b in Range(H), reduce to positive definite restriction H_R and beta=sqrt(b^T H^dagger b). Standard conjugate-norm scalar minimization gives -infinity for a<beta; for a>beta value delta sqrt(a^2-beta^2), t=delta a/Delta and z=-(delta/Delta)H^dagger b + ker(H); when a=beta>0 the infimum 0 is unattained; a=beta=0 iff b=0 and every point is optimal. The Lorentz dual has equation H^(1/2)u=b, hence dual feasibility iff b is in range and a>=beta, with minimum-norm u=(H^dagger)^(1/2)b and dual cone coordinate nu=-sqrt(a^2-beta^2). This covers H=0, b=0, negative a, and all singular ranks. Independently for H=diag(9,0), b=(6,0), a=5,delta=5, the claimed value 5sqrt21 and unrestricted null component verify; b with nonzero null component creates an unbounded ray. This is exact reduction proof, not a numerical extrapolation.
